nodes.summary: The adversary forces $n$ misses while the optimum misses at most $k + \lceil n / k \rceil$ times. Let $k \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a deterministic online pager with cache size $k$ on the $k + 1$ pages $0, \dots, k$. For every $n$, on the adversary's sequence of $n$ requests started from the initial state of $A$, the pager $A$ started in its initial state misses exactly $n$ times, and the furthest-in-future strategy…
nodes.title: The adversary forces $n$ misses while the optimum misses at most $k + \lceil n / k \rceil$ times

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a deterministic online pager with cache size $k$ on the $k + 1$ pages $0, \dots, k$. From a state $q$ of $A$, the adversary's sequence of $n$ requests is empty for $n = 0$; for $n + 1$ it first requests the smallest page not in the cache of $q$ (page $0$ if there is none) and then continues with the adversary's sequence of $n$ requests from the state that $A$ reaches from $q$ by serving that request.
nodes.title: The paging adversary

nodes.summary: A deterministic online paging algorithm with cache size `k`: a state machine whose cache never holds more than `k` pages. Its moves need not be legal transitions; the lower bound holds for any such machine.
nodes.title: Deterministic online paging algorithm

nodes.summary: If a list $c$ of pages has no duplicates and at most $k$ entries, then for every finite request sequence $\sigma$ the cache obtained from $c$ by serving the requests of $\sigma$ in order, each with one FIFO step of capacity $k$, also has no duplicates and at most $k$ entries.
nodes.title: FIFO keeps the cache legal on every request sequence

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $\sigma$ be a finite request sequence, and let $c_0$ be a list of at most $k$ distinct pages. Let $m$ be the number of misses of the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ serving $\sigma$ from the cache $c_0$. Then the FIFO online pager with capacity $k$, started in any legal cache (at most $k$ distinct pages), misses at most $k m + k$ of the requests of $\sigma$.
nodes.title: FIFO is `k`-competitive against the offline optimum

nodes.summary: FIFO is `k`-competitive (Sleator and Tarjan). Let $k \ge 1$, and let $\tau$ be a legal trace of the caching system with capacity $k$ that starts from a cache $c_0$ of at most $k$ distinct pages; let $m$ be its number of misses. Then the FIFO online pager with capacity $k$, started in any legal cache (at most $k$ distinct pages) and serving the requests of $\tau$ in order, misses at most $k m + k$ times.
nodes.title: FIFO is `k`-competitive

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a list of at most $k$ distinct pages (the pages already in the current phase), let $c$ be any list of pages (a FIFO cache, oldest page first), and let $L$ be a list of distinct pages, each of them in $S$, that is a suffix of $c$. For every request sequence $\sigma$, let $P$ be the phase split off from $\sigma$ given $S$: the longest prefix of $\sigma$ whose distinct pages, together with those of $S$,…
nodes.title: FIFO misses at most `k` times per phase

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and let $c$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $c < k d$. For every natural number $b$ there is a finite request sequence $\sigma$ over $k + 1$ pages with $c \cdot m + b < d \cdot f$, where $m$ is the number of misses of the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ serving $\sigma$ from the empty cache, and $f$ is the number of misses of the FIFO online pager with capacity $k$ serving $\sigma$ from…
nodes.title: The ratio `k` is tight for FIFO

nodes.summary: For every legal cache $q$ of capacity $k$ (at most $k$ distinct pages) and every request sequence $\sigma$, the number of misses of the FIFO online pager started in $q$ and serving $\sigma$ equals the number of misses of the policy given by the FIFO step with capacity $k$ serving $\sigma$ from the cache $q$.
nodes.title: FIFO as an online pager misses as often as the FIFO step policy

nodes.summary: The online pager with capacity $k$ whose states are the legal caches of capacity $k$ (lists of at most $k$ distinct pages, oldest first), whose initial state is the empty cache, whose cache in a state is that list itself, and which serves a request $p$ by one FIFO step with capacity $k$.
nodes.title: FIFO paging as an online pager

nodes.summary: If a list $c$ of pages has no duplicates and at most $k$ entries, then for every page $p$ the cache produced from $c$ by one FIFO step with capacity $k$ on request $p$ also has no duplicates and at most $k$ entries.
nodes.title: One FIFO step keeps the cache legal

nodes.summary: The cache is a list of pages, oldest first, and $k$ is the capacity. On a request for a page $p$ already in the cache $c$, the cache stays $c$. Otherwise $p$ is appended at the back of $c$; if $c$ had fewer than $k$ pages, that is the new cache, and if not, the front page, the one loaded earliest, is removed as well.
nodes.title: One step of FIFO paging

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $c$ be a list of $k$ distinct pages and let $f$ be any list of requests. Then the search through $c$ for the first page that does not occur among the first $k - 1$ entries of $f$ succeeds; in particular, some page of $c$ does not occur there.
nodes.title: A full cache has a page outside the next $k - 1$ requests

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ of pages and a capacity $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a legal cache is a list of pages of $\alpha$ with no duplicates and at most $k$ entries.
nodes.title: Legal cache

nodes.summary: LRU as an online pager.
nodes.title: LRU as an online pager

nodes.summary: For a capacity $k$, a cache $c$ (a list of pages, most recently used first) and a request sequence $\sigma$, this is the cache obtained from $c$ by applying one LRU step with capacity $k$ for each request of $\sigma$, in order.
nodes.title: Cache after LRU serves a request sequence

nodes.summary: For a capacity $k$, a cache $c$ (a list of pages, most recently used first) and a requested page $p$, the LRU event is a hit on $p$ if $p \in c$. Otherwise it is a miss on $p$ that evicts the last page of $c$ (the least recently used one) if $c$ is nonempty, $k > 0$ and $c$ has at least $k$ pages, and a miss on $p$ without eviction in all other cases.
nodes.title: The event of an LRU step

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, and let $c$ and $c_0$ be duplicate-free caches with at most $k$ pages each. For every request sequence $\sigma$, the trace that LRU with capacity $k$ emits when serving $\sigma$ from $c$ has at most $k m + k$ misses, where $m$ is the number of misses of the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ serving $\sigma$ from $c_0$.
nodes.title: LRU is $k$-competitive against the offline optimum

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and let $c$ be a duplicate-free cache with at most $k$ pages. Let $e$ be a legal trace of the cache system with capacity $k$ that starts from a duplicate-free cache with at most $k$ pages, and let $m$ be its number of misses. Then the trace that LRU with capacity $k$ emits when serving, from $c$, the requests of $e$ in order has at most $k m + k$ misses.
nodes.title: LRU is $k$-competitive

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $c$ a cache (most recently used first) and $S$ a duplicate-free list of at most $k$ pages equal to the first $|S|$ pages of $c$. For every request sequence $\sigma$, let $\pi$ be the phase that the phase split cuts from $\sigma$ with $S$ as the pages already in the phase: the longest prefix of $\sigma$ whose distinct pages, together with those of $S$, number at most $k$. Then the number of…
nodes.title: LRU misses at most $k - |S|$ times in the rest of a phase

nodes.summary: For a capacity $k$, a cache $c$ and a request sequence $\sigma$, this is the number of requests of $\sigma$ that are not in the current cache when they are served, where the cache starts at $c$ and after each request is updated by one LRU step with capacity $k$.
nodes.title: Number of LRU misses

nodes.summary: For every cache $c$ of at most $k$ pages and every request sequence $\sigma$, the number of misses of LRU with capacity $k$, viewed as an online pager and started in the state with cache $c$, on $\sigma$ equals the number of misses of LRU with capacity $k$ started with cache $c$ on $\sigma$.
nodes.title: LRU as an online pager has LRU's miss count

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $c$ a cache (most recently used first) and $S$ a list of at most $k$ pages equal to the first $|S|$ pages of $c$. If $p \in S$, then after one LRU step with capacity $k$ serving $p$, the first $|S|$ pages of the cache are $p$ followed by $S$ with the first occurrence of $p$ removed.
nodes.title: The recency invariant for a repeated page

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $c$ a cache (most recently used first) and $S$ a list with $|S| + 1 \le k$ equal to the first $|S|$ pages of $c$. If $p \notin S$, then after one LRU step with capacity $k$ serving $p$, the first $|S| + 1$ pages of the cache are $p$ followed by $S$.
nodes.title: The recency invariant for a new page

nodes.summary: For a capacity $k$, a cache $c$ (a list of pages, most recently used first) and a requested page $p$, the LRU step removes the first occurrence of $p$ from $c$ (if any), puts $p$ at the front, and keeps the first $k$ pages of the result. On a miss with a cache of exactly $k \ge 1$ pages, this evicts the last page, the least recently used one.
nodes.title: One LRU step

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity and $c$ a duplicate-free cache with at most $k$ pages. For every page $p$, the cache system with capacity $k$ has a transition from $c$, labelled by the LRU event for $p$ at $c$, to the cache produced by one LRU step with capacity $k$ serving $p$.
nodes.title: Each LRU step is a legal transition

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $c$ a cache given as a list of pages without repetitions with at most $k$ pages, and $\sigma$ a request sequence. Then the sequence of events that LRU emits when serving $\sigma$ from $c$ is a run of the cache system with capacity $k$ from $c$ to the cache LRU holds after serving $\sigma$; the pages requested by these events are exactly $\sigma$, in order; and the number of misses among these…
nodes.title: LRU is a legal cache manager

nodes.summary: Given a capacity $k$, a cache $c$ and a request sequence $\sigma$, the events LRU emits on $\sigma$ from $c$: nothing on the empty sequence, and on a sequence $p$ followed by $\sigma'$, the event LRU emits when serving $p$ from $c$, followed by the events LRU emits on $\sigma'$ from the cache after one LRU step with capacity $k$ serving $p$ from $c$.
nodes.title: The LRU trace

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a list of $k$ distinct pages among the $k + 1$ pages $0, \dots, k$, let $p$ be a page not in $c$, and let $v$ be any page. Then every page $x \neq v$ lies in the cache obtained from $c$ by removing $v$ and adding $p$.
nodes.title: After a miss on a full cache, every page except the evicted one is present

nodes.summary: The pager misses every request of the adversary's sequence.
nodes.title: The pager misses every request

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, let $c$ be a cache and let $w$ be a request sequence all of whose requests lie in $c$. Then for every request sequence $\tau$, the offline strategy with capacity $k$ (on a miss with a full cache, evict the first cached page not among the next $k - 1$ requests, if there is one) started with cache $c$ misses as many times on $w$ followed by $\tau$ as on $\tau$ alone.
nodes.title: Hits do not change the offline strategy's misses

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and consider the $k + 1$ pages $0, 1, \dots, k$. Let $N$ be a natural number, $\sigma$ a sequence of $n \le N$ requests to these pages, and $c$ a cache of $|c| \le k$ distinct pages. Then the number of misses of the offline trace with cache size $k$ from $c$ on $\sigma$ is at most $(k - |c|) + \lfloor (n + k - 1) / k \rfloor = (k - |c|) + \lceil n / k \rceil$: after at most $k - |c|$ misses filling…
nodes.title: The offline trace misses at most once every $k$ requests

nodes.summary: For an online pager $A$, a state $q$ and a request sequence $\sigma$, the number of misses of $A$ from $q$ on $\sigma$ counts the requests of $\sigma$ that are not in the cache of the current state, where the run starts at $q$ and each request moves $A$ to its next state.
nodes.title: Misses of an online pager

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a deterministic online pager with cache size $k$ on the $k + 1$ pages $0, \dots, k$. For a request sequence $\sigma$, write $A(\sigma)$ for the number of misses of $A$ started in its initial state on $\sigma$, and $\mathrm{OPT}(\sigma)$ for the number of misses of the furthest-in-future strategy with capacity $k$ started with an empty cache on $\sigma$. Then for all natural numbers $c$,…
nodes.title: No deterministic online pager is better than $k$-competitive

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $c$ be a cache of at most $k$ distinct pages, let $p$ be a requested page and let $f$ be the list of future requests. Then the event and the new cache produced by the offline step with cache size $k$ on $c$, $p$ and $f$ form a legal transition from $c$ of the caching system with capacity $k$.
nodes.title: Each offline step is a legal transition

nodes.summary: Given a cache size $k$, a cache $c$ (a list of pages), a requested page $p$ and the list $f$ of future requests, the offline step returns an event and a new cache. If $p \in c$, it is a hit on $p$ and the cache is unchanged. Otherwise, if $c$ has fewer than $k$ pages, it is a miss on $p$ with no eviction and the new cache is $p$ followed by $c$. Otherwise, if some page of $c$ does not occur among the first $k - 1$…
nodes.title: Offline paging step

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $c$ be a cache of at most $k$ distinct pages and let $\sigma$ be a list of requests. Then the offline trace with cache size $k$ from $c$ on $\sigma$ is a legal run of the caching system with capacity $k$ from $c$ to some final cache, and the pages served by its events are, in order, exactly $\sigma$.
nodes.title: The offline trace is legal

nodes.summary: Given a cache size $k$, the offline trace from a cache $c$ on a list of requests is defined by recursion on the list: on the empty list it is empty, and on a list with first request $p$ and remaining requests $r$ it is the event of the offline step with cache size $k$ on $c$, $p$ and $r$, followed by the offline trace on $r$ from the new cache of that step.
nodes.title: Offline paging trace

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $c$ be a list of at most $k$ pages from $\{0, \dots, k\}$. Then the outside page of $c$ does not occur in $c$.
nodes.title: The outside page is not cached

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$ and a list $c$ of pages from $\{0, \dots, k\}$, the outside page of $c$ is the smallest $x \in \{0, \dots, k\}$ that does not occur in $c$, or $0$ if every page of $\{0, \dots, k\}$ occurs in $c$.
nodes.title: Outside page of a cache

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, let $s$ be a list of pages without repetitions with at most $k$ pages (the pages already in the current phase), and let $\sigma$ be a request sequence. If the remainder left after splitting off a phase from $\sigma$ given $s$ starts with a page $q$, then there is a list $S$ of exactly $k$ pairwise distinct pages, none equal to $q$, each of which lies in $s$ or in that phase.
nodes.title: A phase ends only on a $(k + 1)$-st distinct page

nodes.summary: Given a capacity $k$ and a list $s$ of pages (the pages already in the current phase, most recent first), a request sequence $\sigma$ is split into a phase and a remainder as follows. The empty sequence splits into two empty parts. For a sequence $p$ followed by $\sigma'$: if $p$ is in $s$, then $p$ joins the phase and $\sigma'$ is split with $s$ replaced by $p$ followed by $s$ with its first occurrence of $p$…
nodes.title: Splitting off a phase

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and consider a paging policy on list caches, given by its step function. Suppose that, started from any cache, the policy misses at most $k$ times on the first phase of every request sequence (the longest prefix of the sequence with at most $k$ distinct pages). Let $T$ be a legal trace of caching with capacity $k$ (a run of the cache transition system) whose initial cache is a list of at most $k$…
nodes.title: A policy that misses at most $k$ times per phase is $k$-competitive

nodes.summary: For every capacity $k$, the misses of the paging policy whose step is the LRU step with capacity $k$ coincide with the LRU misses with capacity $k$, from every starting cache and on every request sequence.
nodes.title: LRU as a policy on list caches

nodes.summary: Let a paging policy be given by its step function, which maps a cache (a list of pages) and a requested page to the next cache. Starting from a cache $c$, the policy serves a request sequence $p_1, \dots, p_n$ by setting $c_0 = c$ and $c_i = \mathrm{step}(c_{i-1}, p_i)$ for each $i$; its number of misses is the number of indices $i$ with $p_i \notin c_{i-1}$.
nodes.title: Misses of a paging policy on list caches

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
